:::{#thm-entropy-chain-rule-n}
#### Chain rule for entropy, many variables

For [discrete random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X_1, \ldots, X_n$
with finite [entropies](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy),

$$\entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_n} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \entropyf{X_i \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{i-1}},$$

where the term for $i = 1$ is $\entropyf{X_1}$.

:::

::: {.proof}

With [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $1$, the tuple $(X_1, \ldots, X_n)$ takes a value $(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ with $\P(X_1=x_1, \ldots, X_n=x_n) > 0$,
so @thm-surprisal-chain-rule-n applies at $(x_1, \ldots, x_n) = (X_1, \ldots, X_n)$:

$$\surprisalf{X_1, \ldots, X_n} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \surprisalf{X_i \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{i-1}}.$$

Every term on the right is nonnegative (@cor-surprisal-discrete-nonnegative),
so the [expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) of the sum is the sum of the expectation of each term:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_n}
&= \E{\surprisalf{X_1, \ldots, X_n}} \\
&= \sum_{i=1}^{n} \E{\surprisalf{X_i \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{i-1}}} \\
&= \sum_{i=1}^{n} \entropyf{X_i \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{i-1}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The first line is @def-joint-entropy, with $(X_1, \ldots, X_{n-1})$ as its first variable and $X_n$ as its second.
The last line is @def-conditional-entropy, with $(X_1, \ldots, X_{i-1})$ as its first variable and $X_i$ as its second,
and @rem-entropy-expected-surprisal for the term $i = 1$.

:::
